title: Word 26 — On Love for One's Neighbor
attribution_note: Word 26 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: The root of love for neighbor

pairs.en: The root and origin of love for neighbor is love for God. Whoever truly loves God will surely love his neighbor as well. Without doubt, God loves every man. So then, whoever truly loves the God who loves, must also love the man whom God loves. *“Let us love one another,”* as God has loved us.

sections.heading: One nature, one Creator, one redemption

pairs.en: God so loved us all that *“He gave His only-begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life”* [John 3:16]. *“Let us also love one another,”* as God has loved us.

sections.heading: The word of God, the one faith, worship in common

pairs.en: All of us are called Christians after Christ: *“let us love one another,”* as He loves us.

sections.heading: One baptism, one renunciation, one hope

pairs.en: All of us have been called to eternal life, and we say in the holy Creed: *“I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the age to come”*: *“let us love one another.”*
To all of us the Heavenly Father, out of His love, gives food, clothing, shelter, and every other good thing: *“let us also love one another.”*
So then, the Christian has reasons enough why he ought to love his neighbor. But the chief reason is this: that God loves man.
Will you curse one whom God blesses?

Christians! It is fearful, exceedingly fearful, to hate one whom God has loved, for whom Christ died and suffered. It is dangerous, exceedingly dangerous, to do evil to one whom God favors, to dishonor one whom God has honored, to curse one whom God has blessed. Therefore, *“let us love one another,”* O Christian, as God has loved us all. Amen.
